title: Distant and lateral opposition

D0.outcome: Explains distant and lateral opposition as the same idea applied at greater distance or along a rank.

D1.outcome: Chooses the king move that keeps or gains the distant opposition in a given K+P position.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, picks between close and distant opposition, including when the defender's own pawn blocks the close form.

D3.outcome: Predicts the result with the opposition on same-colour squares and checks with the tablebase.

misconceptions: Opposition means standing opposite the king.
sources: sources/sheets/edlasker_chess-strategy.md §4 K23 (distant opposition on same-colour squares)
conditions: Kings on the same line with the same-coloured squares; the side to move gives way.
The close form cannot always be used; distant opposition saves the draw.
contrasts: Close opposition that the defender's own pawn blocks.
The author's wording (even gap, side to move) differs from modern usage, and students mix the two.
The pawn's distance when it cannot be captured.
